la:noun:somnus.html:
somnus, i, m.
Sanscr. svap-nas; Gr. ὕπνος; som-nus for sop-nus; cf.: sopor, sopio
.
Lit., sleep: hostes vino domiti somnoque sepulti, Enn. ap. (Ann. v. 291 Vahl.); : vix aegro cum corde meo me somnus reliquit, Enn. ap. (Ann. v. 52 Vahl.); cf., on the contrary: pandite sulti' genas et corde relinquite somnum, id. ap. Müll. (Ann. v. 521 Vahl.): somnum capere,; cf. : somnum videre,: Caninius suo toto consulatu somnum non vidit,: somnum tenere,: somno se dare,: me artior quam solebat somnus complexus est,: puella somno fessa,: somno vincta,; ; : hos oppressos somno,: ne me e somno excitetis,: so, ex somno excitare aliquem,: e somno suscitari,: somno solutus sum,: cum ergo est somno sevocatus animus a societate,: palpebrae somno coniventes,: somno languidus,: in somnis aliquid videre, in sleep, in dreams, Enn. ap. Müll. (Ann. v. 228 Vahl.); cf. ; Poët. ap. ; ; ; ; ; 2, 70, 144; ; ; ; so, less freq.: per somnum,; ; ; and: per somnos,; cf.: ea si cui in somno accidant, Att. ap. : datur in somnum euntibus,: somnum petiere,; : ducere somnos,i. e. protract slumber, continue to sleep, (cf.: trahere quietem,); so, educere somnos,; but: pocula ducentia somnos,causing sleep,: verba placidos facientia somnos,: nuces somnum faciunt,: odor somnum gignit,: somnum parere,: adferre,: conciliare (opp. fugare),: concitare,: adlicere,: somnos invitare,: adimere,: avertere,: rumpere,: perturbare,.— Poet.: conditque natantia lumina somnus,: labi ut somnum sensit in artus,: serpens,: graviore somno premi,: voltus in somnum cadit,: somno cedere,: lumina mergere somno,: somnus altus,: somni faciles,; cf.: somno mollior herba,: somni pingues,; : plenus,: intermissus,: lenis et placidus,: gravis,: servus ad somnum,who keeps watch during one's sleep,.—Personified: Somnus, as a divinity, son of Erebus and Nox, Hyg. Fab. praef.; ; ; ; sq.; ; —
Esp., in reproachful sense, sleep, sloth, drowsiness, inactivity, slumber, idleness, etc.: corde relinquite somnum, Enn. ap. Müll. (Ann. v. 521 Vahl.): dediti ventri ac somno,: somno et conviviis et delectationi nati,: somno et luxu pudendus, : somno indulsit,: dediti somno ciboque,; .—
Poet., transf.
Night: Libra die somnique pares ubi fecerit horas,; cf. . —
Death (mostly with adjj.): longus,: componit lumina somno,: niger,: frigidus,; SO, SOMNO AETERNO SACRVM,: REQVIESCIT IN SOMNO PACIS,.—
Of a calm at sea: pigro torpebant aequora somno,: imbelli recubant litora somno,. —
A dream: exterrita somno, Enn. ap. (Ann. v. 37 Vahl.): promissa somni,.

la:verb:somnio.html:
somnĭo, āvi, ātum, 1, v. a. (
dep. collat. form: hic aedes non somniatur,) [somnium], to dream; to dream of or see in a dream (freq. and class.).
Lit.: mirum atque inscitum somniavi somnium,; so, somnium,; : aliquid (in somnis),; ; ; ; ; cf. aurum,: ovum,: speciem fortunae querentis,; cf.: me somnies, me exspectes, de me cogites,.— With obj.-clause: videbar somniare med ego esse mortuum, Enn. ap. (Epich. v. 1, p. 167 Vahl.); ; ; init.; ; ; —With de: hanc credo causam de illo somniandi fuisse,: puer, de quo somniasset,.—Absol.: totas noctes somniamus,; ; ; —Impers. pass.: Aristoteles et Fabianus plurimum somniari circa ver et auctumnum tradunt,. —
Transf., as in Engl. to dream, i. e. to think idly or vainly, to talk foolishly: eho, quae tu somnias! Hic homo non sanus est,what are you dreaming about?: quos Summanos somnias?: de Lanuvino Phameae erravi; Trojanum somniabam,: ineptias,: ah stulte! tu de Psaltriā me somnias Agere,; .—Absol.: vigilans somniat,; : portenta non disserentium philosophorum sed somniantium,.

la:noun:somnium.html:
somnĭum, ii, n.
id.
.
Lit., a dream, ; ; ; ; Lact. Opif. Dei, 18: rex Priamus somnio perculsus, Enn. ap. (Trag. v. 59 Vahl.): dum huic conicio somnium,interpret,; cf. : interpretes somniorum,: jucundissima somnia,: per somnia loquentes,talking in their sleep,; cf.: quae somnio visa fuerant, Weissenb.—
Personified: Somnia, dreams, as divinities, ; ; sq—
Transf.
For any thing idle, silly, or without foundation (cf. somnio, II.), a dream, an idle whim or fancy, stuff, nonsense: tu, quantus quantus, nihil nisi sapientia es: Ille somnium,: de argento, somnium,; .—Plur.: fabulae! ... logi! ... somnia!: et vigilans stertis nec somnia cernere cessas,visions,; cf. : spes inanes et velut somnia quaedam vigilantium,: exposui fere non philosophorum judicia, sed delirantium somnia, : Chrysippus Stoicorum somniorum vaferrimus interpres,: leviter curare videtur, Quo promissa cadant et somnia Pythagorea,.—
Poet.: Somnus, tibi somnia tristia portans,i. e. fatal sleep,.

la:adj:somnifer.html:
somnĭfer, ĕra, ĕrum, adj.
somnus-fero
,
sleep-bringing, soporific, somniferous (poet. and in post-Aug. prose): vis papaveris,: virga (Mercurii),: aspis,causing torpidity, deadly,; so, venenum (aspidis),: strychnos,; cf. somniculosus, II., and somnificus.

la:adj:somniculosus.html:
somnĭcŭlōsus, a, um, adj.
somnus
,
full of sleep, i. e.
Pass., inclined to sleep, drowsy, dozy, sleepy, sluggish, slothful (rare

but class.; cf. sopitus): quae vitia non sunt senectutis, sed inertis, ignavae, somniculosae senectutis,: villicus,: genus mancipiorum (with socors),: glires,: Etesiae,.—

Act., making sleepy, drowsy, or sluggish: aspis, i. e. causing torpor or numbness, palsying, deadly (cf. somnifer and somnificus), Cinna ap. ; Laber. ap. (Com. Fragm. 86 Rib.).—Adv.: somnĭ-cŭlōsē (acc. to I.), sleepily, lazily, sluggishly: persequi eri imperia,: agere aliquid,.
